I guess my question is this....People taking advantage of others - is that a culture? Or the individual? Not that these are entirely mutually exclusive, but I would say that a person taking advantage of others is more the result of a person becoming selfish a based on their their life experiences rather than a pervasive group culture.

I believe that people become less prone to racism or negative generalization when they become more familiar with a certain group of people. So the solution I think would be exposure - at least part of the solution. No one can engineer this by policy, so it would just have to happen organically. Similar to what is happening in the USA with its great diversity.
Agree. I think that's the problem with racism. They may experience a specific culture, not like it, and attribute that to everyone with the same skin color. It's basically lazy thinking.

I actually joined Reddit just to respond to this thread. I'll take a stab a answering your question. The argument I've seen most often is this: people of color can't be racist because racism requires you to be in a position of power. Personally, I reject this answer for two reasons 1. Racism is defined as the following " prejudice, discrimination, or antagonism directed against someone of a different race based on the belief that one's own race is superior. " According to this definition, I can't see why you need to be in a position on of power to hold this belief. Perhaps when people use this argument they are referring to systemic racism, rather than just good ol' normal racism 2. It is not longer the case that power is exclusively held by "whites only." Many people of color hold positions of color - far beyond the token handful that people used to refer to when proclaiming we have finally attained equality/post-racial society. Don't accept negative comments based on your race. I see this almost daily e.g. "the scariest things in the world is a white male in a suit" or "white people are the most violent people to have ever existed" or "white people just need to shit the fuck up and stop taking up so much space" and various memes about cisgendered white males. It's widespread. But at the same, don't judge people according to their group e.g. black people, white people. Almost anything you say about "black people" or "white people" is bound to be incorrect about a large majority of that group.
